slot.brief: In a spinel or ionic solid of fcc oxide ions with ions in tetrahedral/octahedral voids, determine the fraction of voids occupied and hence the formula.

stem: An fcc array of oxide ions contains one $\text{A}^{2+}$ ion in tetrahedral voids per unit cell. $\text{B}^{3+}$ ions occupy half the octahedral voids. What fraction of octahedral voids is occupied, and what is the formula of the solid?

verdicts.working: An fcc unit cell has 4 oxide ions and 4 octahedral voids. Half occupied means 2 B ions; with 1 A ion, the ratio A:B:O is 1:2:4, giving AB₂O₄.

working:
fcc unit cell: $4\ \text{O}^{2-}$ ions, $8$ tetrahedral voids, $4$ octahedral voids.
$N_A=1$; $N_B=\dfrac{1}{2}(4)=2$.
Fraction of octahedral voids occupied $=\dfrac{2}{4}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.
$A:B:O=1:2:4$; formula $=\text{AB}_2\text{O}_4$.

Independent check: An fcc unit cell has 4 oxide ions and 4 octahedral voids. Half occupied means 2 B ions; with 1 A ion, the ratio A:B:O is 1:2:4, giving AB₂O₄.
solution:
An fcc unit cell contains $4$ oxide ions and $4$ octahedral voids. Half of the octahedral voids are occupied, so $N_B=\frac{1}{2}(4)=2$.
The ion ratio is $A:B:O=1:2:4$, giving the formula $\text{AB}_2\text{O}_4$.
